# 2 Chronicles Chapter 4 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** He made an altar of bronze, twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.

**2** Then he made the cast metal sea. It was round, ten cubits from rim to rim, five cubits high, and thirty cubits in circumference.

**3** Under it were figures of oxen all around it, encircling it, ten to a cubit, in two rows, cast when it was cast.

**4** It stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The sea was set on them, and all their hindquarters were inward.

**5** Its thickness was a handbreadth. Its rim was made like the rim of a cup, like the flower of a lily. It held three thousand baths.

**6** He also made ten basins for washing and set five on the right side and five on the left. In them the things to be used for the burnt offerings were rinsed, but the sea was for the priests to wash in.

**7** And he made ten golden lampstands as prescribed, and set them in the temple, five on the right side and five on the left.

**8** He also made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the right side and five on the left. And he made a hundred basins of gold.

**9** He made the court of the priests and the great court and doors for the court, and he overlaid their doors with bronze.

**10** He set the sea on the right side of the house toward the southeast.

**11** Huram also made the pots, the shovels, and the basins. So Huram finished the work that he did for King Solomon in the house of God:

**12** the two pillars, the bowls, and the two capitals on the top of the pillars; and the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals on the top of the pillars;

**13** and the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks — two rows of pomegranates for each network — to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the pillars.

**14** He made the stands and the basins on the stands;

**15** the one sea and the twelve oxen under it;

**16** and the pots, the shovels, the forks, and all the associated vessels — Huram-abi made them of polished bronze for King Solomon for the house of the LORD.

**17** In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.

**18** Solomon made all these vessels in great quantities, for the weight of the bronze could not be determined.

**19** So Solomon made all the vessels that were in the house of God: the golden altar, the tables for the bread of the Presence,

**20** the lampstands with their lamps of pure gold, to burn before the inner sanctuary as prescribed;

**21** the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs — of purest gold;

**22** the snuffers, basins, dishes for incense, and firepans — of pure gold; and the entrance of the house, the inner doors to the Most Holy Place and the doors of the main hall of the temple — of gold.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

No significant council discussion for this chapter.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1
- **EMET:** "And-he-made an-altar-of bronze twenty cubits its-length and-twenty cubits its-width and-ten cubits its-height."
- **LOGOS:** "He made an altar of bronze, twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high."
- **PNEUMA:** "Solomon made a bronze altar twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high."
- **SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus baseline.

### V.2
- **EMET:** "And-he-made the-sea cast ten in-the-cubit from-its-rim to its-rim round all-around and-five in-the-cubit its-height and-"
- **LOGOS:** "Then he made the cast metal sea. It was round, ten cubits from rim to rim, five cubits high, and thirty cubits in circum"
- **PNEUMA:** "He then cast the great bronze basin called the Sea — circular, ten cubits from rim to rim, five cubits high, and thirty "
- **SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus baseline.

### V.3
- **EMET:** "And-likeness-of oxen under-it all-around surrounding it ten in-the-cubit surrounding the-sea all-around two rows-of the-"
- **LOGOS:** "Under it were figures of oxen all around it, encircling it, ten to a cubit, in two rows, cast when it was cast."
- **PNEUMA:** "Below the rim, figures of oxen encircled it — ten per cubit, in two rows, cast as one piece with the basin."
- **SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus baseline.

### V.5
- **EMET:** "And-its-thickness a-handbreadth and-its-rim like-work-of rim-of a-cup flower-of a-lily holding baths three-thousand it-c"
- **LOGOS:** "Its thickness was a handbreadth. Its rim was made like the rim of a cup, like the flower of a lily. It held three thousa"
- **PNEUMA:** "The basin was a handbreadth thick, with a rim shaped like a lily blossom. It could hold three thousand baths of water."
- **SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus baseline.

### V.10
- **EMET:** "And-the-sea he-set from-the-side the-right from-the-front toward-the-south-east."
- **LOGOS:** "He set the sea on the right side of the house toward the southeast."
- **PNEUMA:** "He positioned the Sea on the south side of the temple, toward the southeast."
- **SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus baseline.

### V.18
- **EMET:** "And-he-made Solomon all the-vessels these in-great abundance for not was-searched-out weight-of the-bronze."
- **LOGOS:** "Solomon made all these vessels in great quantities, for the weight of the bronze could not be determined."
- **PNEUMA:** "Solomon made so many of these objects that the total weight of the bronze was never calculated."
- **SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus baseline.

*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
